# Origin

> Origin is the evidence layer for high-consequence AI agents. The implemented public Agent Reference Check evaluates a bound configuration against deterministic synthetic support and IAM tasks. It produces a tamper-evident demo artifact that can be rechecked offline. The deterministic oracle is the sole grading authority; an LLM does not grade another LLM.
>
> Current boundary: browser-local synthetic evaluation, session-signed and unpinned evidence, execution not attempted. A valid demo signature does not establish trusted Origin issuance, customer deployment, production readiness, or certification. Runtime enforcement and a controlled tool-call proxy remain proposed pilot architecture, not deployed general capabilities.

## Implemented public workflow
1. Bind the model, tools, policy, budget, and scenario battery into the evaluation configuration.
2. Challenge deterministic policy logic with synthetic tasks.
3. Grade the decisions with the deterministic oracle.
4. Produce a configuration-bound, browser-session-signed demo artifact.
5. Reverify supported artifact checks offline. Changing a bound field produces a configuration-drift failure (VOID).

The public demo does not execute production actions, connect a customer's agent to a live tool-call proxy, or establish trusted issuer identity. Artifact integrity, policy evaluation, and release authority are separate questions.

## Audience and engagement
Origin is a working prototype seeking design partners among agent-platform, security, trust, and infrastructure teams reviewing high-consequence agent workflows. The first wedge is internal-ops and production-access agents. No active customer pilot is claimed.

A founder-led Agent Evidence Review starts with one workflow, the intended configuration, and the reviewer's approval question. The review scopes the evaluation and identifies missing evidence. Customer data, pilot integrations, runtime controls, and deployment-specific terms require separate authorization and agreement. No customer deployment or reviewer acceptance is claimed.

## Proposed architecture
A future controlled execution path would place permission, scope, budget, policy, and approval checks between an agent proposal and a side effect. A controlled proxy, runtime enforcement, named approvals, and kill switches are proposed pilot architecture. They are not current general production capabilities.

Model proposes. Environment executes. Verifier evaluates. Gate decides. Trace proves. Capability is not permission.

## Evidence ladder
- TR-A001: authored specimen of the evidence-package format. Illustrative, not a machine-emitted run. See /proof#tr-a001.
- TR-A002: machine-emitted sandbox trace, available now. Twelve events with a re-verifiable SHA-256 chain; final digest ca1d4690206e4dcf3d654b907d02d2bccf9bcdc16ddc555071fec21874578b32. Download /proof/tr-a002.json and recheck with npm run proof:verify. No live money, customer data, performance claim, or reviewer acceptance. See /proof#tr-a002.
- TR-A003: first external design-partner trace, not earned yet. No data is published for it.

## Evidence boundaries
“Tamper-evident” means the relevant integrity check can detect alteration under its bindings. It does not establish universal safety or correctness. “Review-ready” means a reviewer can inspect the evidence; it does not mean a reviewer has accepted it. Origin is decision-support and evidence infrastructure, not production SaaS, legal advice, or compliance certification.

Keep authored specimens, machine-emitted sandbox traces, synthetic evaluations, generated counterfactuals, authorized fixtures, and approved real customer evidence distinct. Real customer readiness remains blocked until separately authorized evidence passes the relevant checks.

## Labs
Labs demonstrates aspects of a common evidence contract in bounded simulations: robot proving ground, warehouse simulation, fleet operations, a mock-vault credential broker, and a sample-floor Foundry workflow. These are research demonstrations, not production products, robot deployment, or robot certification.

The public Foundry uses a browser-local sample. Image upload and provider-backed operations are disabled publicly. Separately enabled local/backend processing requires affirmative consent and the privacy-policy disclosures.

The RSI dashboard publishes a research snapshot from a pinned private pipeline. Its metrics are not re-derivable from this public repository. Learned-policy results use route-summary/map-derived features, not raw end-to-end perception. Oracle-recovery upper bounds are labeled separately from learned results. Synthetic demos and generated counterfactuals do not establish real customer readiness. Proprietary algorithm implementation is outside this public repository.

Generated brand imagery and footage are illustrations, not product recordings, company facilities, or customer evidence.
